method: Triton ELF load + instruction emulation with syscall stubs; stdin data bytes tainted; taint checked at stores into canary_after
notes: Drove nft_byteorder_eval directly (RIP=0x403017, args built in memory) to bypass static-glibc startup; emulated the real function plus the nft_expr_priv/htons leaf helpers linked into the binary. The size==2 / NTOH loop runs len/2=40 iterations at stride 4; the last 20 stores (canary_after offsets +0..+76, all at PC 0x4034ca) land in the sentinel -> Triton SEES the spatial OOB write (n_oob_writes=20). However, with sreg=dreg=0 those OOB iterations read their source from regs+80.. == canary_after, which the harness fills with a CONSTANT pattern (0xCDEF), not stdin. Triton's movzwl zero-extend load clears the destination register taint, so the byteswapped value written OOB (0xEFCD) carries NO color-A taint: n_oob_writes_tainted=0. In-bounds iterations i=0..19 (writes into regs) DO produce tainted stores, confirming taint propagation through movzwl->htons(rol)->store works. This diverges from the DBI microtaint reference (20 tainted): microtaint over-taints because its movzwl load from the untainted canary does not clear the stale taint left in ax by the last in-bounds iteration -- the known movzx taint-clearing subtlety. Triton is register-precise here and reports the OOB values as constant-derived, not attacker-derived. reached_ret=True steps=1026.

extra.propagation_positive_control: 20/20 in-bounds loop stores (into regs) carry attacker taint -> taint propagation verified; OOB stores are untainted only because their source is the constant canary (written value 0xefcd == byteswap of 0xcdef, not stdin 0x42)
extra.divergence_from_microtaint: microtaint reports 20 tainted OOB writes; Triton reports 0. The OOB values are byteswapped constant-canary bytes, provably not stdin: microtaint over-taints via stale-ax carry-over across the untainted movzwl load (movzx taint-clear artifact); Triton clears it.
